+++ b/js/common/guestValidationPath.js
@@ -0,0 +1,301 @@
+/**
+ * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
+ * dead-zone fixes.
+ *
+ * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
+ * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
+ * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
+ *
+ *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
+ *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
+ *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
+ *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
+ *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
+ *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
+ *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
+ *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
+ *      (checks: green) never matches either.
+ *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
+ *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
+ *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
+ *
+ * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
+ * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
+ * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
+ * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
+ * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
+ * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
+ * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
+ *
+ * Exports:
+ *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
+ *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
+ *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
+ *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
+ *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
+ *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
+ *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
+ *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
+ *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: the head is decided
+ *       (real >= 1, the fa#923 undecided-head guard) and red === 0. A
+ *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
+ *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
+ *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
+ *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
+ *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
+ *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
+ *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
+ *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
+ *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
+ *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
+ *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
+ *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
+ *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
+ *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
+ *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
+ *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
+ *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
+ *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
+ *       blocked drop out.
+ *
+ * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
+ * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
+ */
+
+'use strict';
+
+var machineAuthorModule = require('./machineAuthor.js');
+
+// Parity with smProvider BOOKKEEPING_CHECK_PREFIXES — passed in by the
+// caller (smAgent forwards smProviderModule.BOOKEEPING_CHECK_PREFIXES so
+// the two lists can never drift); this default only keeps the module
+// usable standalone.
+var DEFAULT_BOOKEEPING_PREFIXES = ['kicker /', 'Wake-up probe', 'merge /'];
+
+var RED_CONCLUSIONS = ['FAILURE', 'TIMED_OUT'];
+var PENDING_STATUSES = ['QUEUED', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'WAITING', 'PENDING'];
+
+// Classify ONE check-run entry (CheckRun name/conclusion/status or
+// StatusContext context/state — same dual read as the provider). Kept in
+// tiny pieces: the crap4js gate (CRAP <= 8) measures every helper, and
+// GraalJS forbids the array combinators that would shrink the branching.
+function _runField(c, primary, fallback) {
+    return (c && (c[primary] || c[fallback])) || null;
+}
+
+function _upperOrNull(v) {
+    return v ? String(v).toUpperCase() : null;
+}
+
+function _normalizeRun(c) {
+    return {
+        name: String(_runField(c, 'name', 'context') || ''),
+        conclusion: _upperOrNull(_runField(c, 'conclusion', 'state')),
+        status: _upperOrNull(c && c.status)
+    };
+}
+
+function _isBookeeping(name, prefixes) {
+    var list = prefixes || DEFAULT_BOOKEEPING_PREFIXES;
+    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
+        if (name.indexOf(list[i]) === 0) return true;
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
+function _isRedConclusion(conclusion) {
+    return !!conclusion && RED_CONCLUSIONS.indexOf(conclusion) !== -1;
+}
+
+function _isPendingRun(conclusion, status) {
+    return !conclusion || PENDING_STATUSES.indexOf(status) !== -1;
+}
+
+// One run → exactly one tally bucket ('bokept' | 'canceled' | 'red' |
+// 'pending' | 'real'). Order is the policy: stubs and CANCELLED are
+// never verdicts; a red conclusion is never also pending.
+function _tallyBucket(c, bookeepingPrefixes) {
+    if (_isBookeeping(c.name, bookeepingPrefixes)) return 'bokept';
+    if (c.conclusion === 'CANCELLED') return 'canceled';
+    if (_isRedConclusion(c.conclusion)) return 'red';
+    if (_isPendingRun(c.conclusion, c.status)) return 'pending';
+    return 'real';
+}
+
+/**
+ * The REAL check-run census of one head.
+ * @param {Array|null} checkRuns raw REST check-runs entries
+ * @param {Array|null} bookeepingPrefixes stub-name prefixes ('merge /', …)
+ * @returns {{red: number, pending: number, real: number, bokept: number,
+ *            canceled: number}} — CANCELLED conclusions and bookeeping
+ *          stubs are never verdicts; a run with no conclusion or a
+ *          queued/in_progress status pends.
+ */
+function realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) {
+    var t = { red: 0, pending: 0, real: 0, bokept: 0, canceled: 0 };
+    if (!checkRuns || !checkRuns.length) return t;
+    for (var i = 0; i < checkRuns.length; i++) {
+        var bucket = _tallyBucket(_normalizeRun(checkRuns[i]), bookeepingPrefixes);
+        if (bucket === 'red' || bucket === 'pending') t.real++;
+        t[bucket]++;
+    }
+    return t;
+}
+
+/** Merge bar: no real red AND no real in-flight check. Null fails closed. */
+function mergeableZeroFailing(tally) {
+    return !!tally && tally.red === 0 && tally.pending === 0;
+}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- **Title**: gh-1133 [SM] Human-authored PRs have no validation/merge path: prMachineAuthor-only arming + guest heads never get real check-runs (3 fa PRs stuck 3h)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1133` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1249
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T05:17:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:54:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1133
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (#1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (`sm_github.json`, directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored armed+approved CLEAN guests with no concluded rollup merge when the head's real check census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` label came from a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- Pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js`: `realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent` — policy unit-tested in isolation.
- Merge gate is fail-closed: real red, in-flight check, active head run, missing arm event or probe error → refuse; `merge / …` stubs and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Guest rung in `update_branch` clears a stale `validation_failed` park when the punished head is decided (≥1 real concluded check) and red-free — `real >= 1` preserves fa#923 sticky-park semantics; machine parks keep gh-750 behavior.
- AC3: cached per-tick dead-zone scan rides the factory-state snapshot (`deadZone`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (#637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

  G --> T[realCheckTally census]

  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm| R[refuse - fail closed]

  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park]
  U -->|undecided / red| H[fa-923 park holds]
  B[blocked guests] --> DZ[deadZone snapshot] --> S[summary counter]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- **Title**: gh-1133 [SM] Human-authored PRs have no validation/merge path: prMachineAuthor-only arming + guest heads never get real check-runs (3 fa PRs stuck 3h)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1133` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1249
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T05:17:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:54:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1133
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (#1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (`sm_github.json`, directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored armed+approved CLEAN guests with no concluded rollup merge when the head's real check census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` label came from a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- Pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js`: `realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent` — policy unit-tested in isolation.
- Merge gate is fail-closed: real red, in-flight check, active head run, missing arm event or probe error → refuse; `merge / …` stubs and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Guest rung in `update_branch` clears a stale `validation_failed` park when the punished head is decided (≥1 real concluded check) and red-free — `real >= 1` preserves fa#923 sticky-park semantics; machine parks keep gh-750 behavior.
- AC3: cached per-tick dead-zone scan rides the factory-state snapshot (`deadZone`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (#637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

  G --> T[realCheckTally census]
  G --> E[isManualArm events probe]
  T -->|zero-failing + manual arm| M[merge_pr]
  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm| R[refuse - fail closed]
  P[parked guest] --> U[update_branch guest rung]
  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park]
  U -->|undecided / red| H[fa-923 park holds]
  B[blocked guests] --> DZ[deadZone snapshot] --> S[summary counter]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- **Title**: gh-1133 [SM] Human-authored PRs have no validation/merge path: prMachineAuthor-only arming + guest heads never get real check-runs (3 fa PRs stuck 3h)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1133` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1249
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T05:17:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:54:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1133
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (#1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (`sm_github.json`, directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored armed+approved CLEAN guests with no concluded rollup merge when the head's real check census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` label came from a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- Pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js`: `realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent` — policy unit-tested in isolation.
- Merge gate is fail-closed: real red, in-flight check, active head run, missing arm event or probe error → refuse; `merge / …` stubs and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Guest rung in `update_branch` clears a stale `validation_failed` park when the punished head is decided (≥1 real concluded check) and red-free — `real >= 1` preserves fa#923 sticky-park semantics; machine parks keep gh-750 behavior.
- AC3: cached per-tick dead-zone scan rides the factory-state snapshot (`deadZone`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (#637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

  G --> T[realCheckTally census]
  G --> E[isManualArm events probe]
  T -->|zero-failing + manual arm| M[merge_pr]
  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm| R[refuse - fail closed]
  P[parked guest] --> U[update_branch guest rung]
  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park]
  U -->|undecided / red| H[fa-923 park holds]
  B[blocked guests] --> DZ[deadZone snapshot] --> S[summary counter]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Wri…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1136
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1136
- **Title**: gh-1133 [SM] Human-authored PRs have no validation/merge path: prMachineAuthor-only arming + guest heads never get real check-runs (3 fa PRs stuck 3h)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1133` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1249
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T05:17:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:54:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1133
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (#1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (`sm_github.json`, directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored armed+approved CLEAN guests with no concluded rollup merge when the head's real check census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` label came from a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- Pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js`: `realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent` — policy unit-tested in isolation.
- Merge gate is fail-closed: real red, in-flight check, active head run, missing arm event or probe error → refuse; `merge / …` stubs and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Guest rung in `update_branch` clears a stale `validation_failed` park when the punished head is decided (≥1 real concluded check) and red-free — `real >= 1` preserves fa#923 sticky-park semantics; machine parks keep gh-750 behavior.
- AC3: cached per-tick dead-zone scan rides the factory-state snapshot (`deadZone`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (#637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Q[merge-validated-guest rule] -->|notMachine + armed + CLEAN + none/pending| G[guestZeroFailingMergeGate]
  G --> T[realCheckTally census]
  G --> E[isManualArm events probe]
  T -->|zero-failing + manual arm| M[merge_pr]
  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm| R[refuse - fail closed]
  P[parked guest] --> U[update_branch guest rung]
  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park]
  U -->|undecided / red| H[fa-923 park holds]
  B[blocked guests] --> DZ[deadZone snapshot] --> S[summary counter]
```

</details>

# PR Diff Truncated

Original size: 78375 characters.
Kept: first 7800 and last 4200 characters.

The full diff is available in the checked-out PR branch. Use `git diff` or CodeGraph for focused source navigation instead of relying only on this file.

```diff
diff --git a/js/common/guestValidationPath.js b/js/common/guestValidationPath.js
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..cf693f18
--- /dev/null
+++ b/js/common/guestValidationPath.js
@@ -0,0 +1,301 @@
+/**
+ * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
+ * dead-zone fixes.
+ *
+ * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
+ * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
+ * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
+ *
+ *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
+ *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
+ *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
+ *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
+ *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
+ *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
+ *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
+ *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
+ *      (checks: green) never matches either.
+ *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
+ *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
+ *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
+ *
+ * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
+ * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
+ * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
+ * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
+ * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
+ * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
+ * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
+ *
+ * Exports:
+ *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
+ *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
+ *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
+ *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
+ *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
+ *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
+ *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
+ *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
+ *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: the head is decided
+ *       (real >= 1, the fa#923 undecided-head guard) and red === 0. A
+ *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
+ *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
+ *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
+ *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
+ *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
+ *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
+ *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
+ *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
+ *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
+ *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
+ *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
+ *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
+ *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
+ *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
+ *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
+ *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
+ *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
+ *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
+ *       blocked drop out.
+ *
+ * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
+ * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
+ * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
+ */
+
+'use strict';
+
+var machineAuthorModule = require('./machineAuthor.js');
+
+// Parity with smProvider BOOKKEEPING_CHECK_PREFIXES — passed in by the
+// caller (smAgent forwards smProviderModule.BOOKEEPING_CHECK_PREFIXES so
+// the two lists can never drift); this default only keeps the module
+// usable standalone.
+var DEFAULT_BOOKEEPING_PREFIXES = ['kicker /', 'Wake-up probe', 'merge /'];
+
+var RED_CONCLUSIONS = ['FAILURE', 'TIMED_OUT'];
+var PENDING_STATUSES = ['QUEUED', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'WAITING', 'PENDING'];
+
+// Classify ONE check-run entry (CheckRun name/conclusion/status or
+// StatusContext context/state — same dual read as the provider). Kept in
+// tiny pieces: the crap4js gate (CRAP <= 8) measures every helper, and
+// GraalJS forbids the array combinators that would shrink the branching.
+function _runField(c, primary, fallback) {
+    return (c && (c[primary] || c[fallback])) || null;
+}
+
+function _upperOrNull(v) {
+    return v ? String(v).toUpperCase() : null;
+}
+
+function _normalizeRun(c) {
+    return {
+        name: String(_runField(c, 'name', 'context') || ''),
+        conclusion: _upperOrNull(_runField(c, 'conclusion', 'state')),
+        status: _upperOrNull(c && c.status)
+    };
+}
+
+function _isBookeeping(name, prefixes) {
+    var list = prefixes || DEFAULT_BOOKEEPING_PREFIXES;
+    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
+        if (name.indexOf(list[i]) === 0) return true;
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
+function _isRedConclusion(conclusion) {
+    return !!conclusion && RED_CONCLUSIONS.indexOf(conclusion) !== -1;
+}
+
+function _isPendingRun(conclusion, status) {
+    return !conclusion || PENDING_STATUSES.indexOf(status) !== -1;
+}
+
+// One run → exactly one tally bucket ('bokept' | 'canceled' | 'red' |
+// 'pending' | 'real'). Order is the policy: stubs and CANCELLED are
+// never verdicts; a red conclusion is never also pending.
+function _tallyBucket(c, bookeepingPrefixes) {
+    if (_isBookeeping(c.name, bookeepingPrefixes)) return 'bokept';
+    if (c.conclusion === 'CANCELLED') return 'canceled';
+    if (_isRedConclusion(c.conclusion)) return 'red';
+    if (_isPendingRun(c.conclusion, c.status)) return 'pending';
+    return 'real';
+}
+
+/**
+ * The REAL check-run census of one head.
+ * @param {Array|null} checkRuns raw REST check-runs entries
+ * @param {Array|null} bookeepingPrefixes stub-name prefixes ('merge /', …)
+ * @returns {{red: number, pending: number, real: number, bokept: number,
+ *            canceled: number}} — CANCELLED conclusions and bookeeping
+ *          stubs are never verdicts; a run with no conclusion or a
+ *          queued/in_progress status pends.
+ */
+function realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) {
+    var t = { red: 0, pending: 0, real: 0, bokept: 0, canceled: 0 };
+    if (!checkRuns || !checkRuns.length) return t;
+    for (var i = 0; i < checkRuns.length; i++) {

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1133
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (#1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (`sm_github.json`, directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored armed+approved CLEAN guests with no concluded rollup merge when the head's real check census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` label came from a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- Pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js`: `realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent` — policy unit-tested in isolation.
- Merge gate is fail-closed: real red, in-flight check, active head run, missing arm event or probe error → refuse; `merge / …` stubs and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Guest rung in `update_branch` clears a stale `validation_failed` park when the punished head is decided (≥1 real concluded check) and red-free — `real >= 1` preserves fa#923 sticky-park semantics; machine parks keep gh-750 behavior.
- AC3: cached per-tick dead-zone scan rides the factory-state snapshot (`deadZone`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (#637/#682 invariants hold).
